oliver: Quick one  our EU office has a local bridge day on Dec 27 but company shutdown is Dec 24Dec 31. Can folks choose to bank that bridge day instead of taking PTO?

hina: same Q from EMEA hiring  new joiner wants to keep the bridge day for travel and not use their limited PTO.

jess (People Ops): short answer: yes, we support a limited timebank/comp-bank for holiday swaps and essential coverage, but it must be pre-approved and recorded. long answer: we have two mechanisms: 1) holiday swap (1:1 day exchange) and 2) timebank (temporary comp hours recorded for work done during the shutdown or for banked local holidays). Timebank is intended for small, documented exceptions and not as a permanent balance.

kevin (Payroll): operational note: timebank hours are tracked separately and must be scheduled/taken within 90 days; they do not count toward carryover cap. if payroll pays out comp instead of time off, that payment will be taxed per local law.

jess (People Ops): operational flow: 
1) employee requests swap or timebank in portal (select "holiday swap" or "timebank request").
2) manager confirms coverage and selects repayment plan (alternate day off or comp payout).
3) people-ops approves and notifies payroll to tag hours as timebank.

oliver: If someone is on unpaid LOA and we ask them to cover interviews, can we add hours to timebank?

jess (People Ops): LOA folks are not required to work. If they volunteer, managers must explicitly offer compensation (timebank or payout) in writing. For unpaid LOA, payroll needs a signed opt-in; we'll code hours as "comp-volunteer".

hina: Is timebank subject to the 40h carryover restriction? Asking because some folks expect it to roll into next year.

kevin (Payroll): no, timebank = separate ledger. It doesn't affect PTO balance or carryover caps. It must be scheduled/taken within 90 days from the accrual date or it expires. Exceptions require manager + people-ops approval and rare payroll sign-off.

jess (People Ops): Emergency carryover: for medical or legally-mandated cases where someone couldn't use PTO because of hospitalization or statutory restriction, we can request a carryover >40h. Docs required and deadline is Jan 31 for standard exceptions; medical exceptions accepted later with paperwork.

oliver: what's the minimal info managers need to include in a timebank request?

jess (People Ops): use this minimal template in the portal (also copy/paste-able): 

```
Timebank request
Employee: <name>
Dates/hours to bank: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD / <hours>
Reason: e.g., local bridge day swap OR worked interviews during shutdown
Manager coverage note: who covers and repayment plan (alternate day off YYYY-MM-DD or payout)
LOA status: active/none/volunteer (if volunteer attach signed opt-in)
Payroll coding: timebank / comp-payout (manager selects)
```

people-ops-bot: Reminder: "Timebank hours expire after 90 days unless exception approved. Carryover cap unchanged; medical exceptions accepted after Jan 31 with docs." <https://hr.redwood.com/timebank>

hina: Example: can we bank 8 hours from Dec 27 and take Jan 15 as the comp day?

jess (People Ops): yes, that's a valid plan. Manager must approve and record Jan 15 as the repayment day in the portal. Payroll will tag the 8 hours on Dec 27 and mark Jan 15 as scheduled comp usage.

oliver: if we accidentally forget to schedule the comp day and it lapses, does payroll auto-pay?

kevin (Payroll): no auto-pay. If it lapses we'll follow up with the manager; if it's clearly an admin error we'll correct and either schedule comp or pay out (with tax implications) after people-ops + finance approval. Avoid lapses by scheduling the repayment before submission completes.

jess (People Ops): final note: timebank is meant to reduce PTO friction for cross-region holidays and essential work during shutdowns. not a substitute for PTO. ping people-ops if you want a pre-check before submitting an unusual case. :handshake:
